batch: Batch 11 — D17 (watchlist live resize) + D18 (single right dock region)
baseline: D1–D16 built and frozen (commit fd0bb0a); this graph is the Batch-11 delta only.

tasks.title: Create the shared chart-area dock-width model ui/dock_layout.py (D17/D18 Phase 1)
tasks.description: Create the pure, Qt-free ui/dock_layout.py holding the single source of truth for dock widths measured against the chart area (the MainWindow central-widget width): constants CHART_MIN_WIDTH=400, WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH=150, DEFAULT_WATCHLIST_WIDTH=220, RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH=200, cap fractions 0.50/0.40, and the pure functions watchlist_max_width(chart_area_w), right_dock_max_width(chart_area_w) and plan_dock_widths(chart_area_w, requested_left, requested_right) -> (left, right) that applies the independent caps and the B3 cross-clamp guaranteeing chart_area >= 400px. Ship its offscreen unit tests.
acceptance_criteria: Given ui/dock_layout.py, When it is imported in an offscreen process, Then it imports no PyQt6, pyqtgraph or other Qt module and needs no QApplication.

Given ui/dock_layout.py, When its constants are read, Then CHART_MIN_WIDTH == 400, WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH == 150, DEFAULT_WATCHLIST_WIDTH == 220, RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH == 200, the watchlist cap fraction is 0.50 and the right-dock cap fraction is 0.40, and CHART_MIN_WIDTH is in agreement with ui/watchlist_panel.CHART_MIN_WIDTH.
Given a chart_area_w, When watchlist_max_width(chart_area_w) is called, Then it returns max(WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH, min(floor(0.50 * chart_area_w), chart_area_w - CHART_MIN_WIDTH)).
Given a chart_area_w, When right_dock_max_width(chart_area_w) is called, Then it returns max(RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH, min(floor(0.40 * chart_area_w), chart_area_w - CHART_MIN_WIDTH)).

Given a chart_area_w and requested left/right widths, When plan_dock_widths(chart_area_w, requested_left, requested_right) is called, Then each returned width is within its own [min, max] cap, and where feasible chart_area_w - left - right >= CHART_MIN_WIDTH; enlarging one requested width forces the other to shrink when the flat caps would starve the chart.

Given the edge cases (a tiny window where the flat cap is below the dock minimum, both docks requested near their individual maxima, and one side requested over budget), When plan_dock_widths is called, Then it never returns a width below the dock minimum, never raises, and returns stable integer widths even when chart_area_w - left - right cannot reach CHART_MIN_WIDTH (the chart minimum yields on an infeasible window; dock minimums win).

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given ui/dock_layout.py, When it is imported in an offscreen process, Then it imports no PyQt6, pyqtgraph or other Qt module and needs no QApplication.
tests.description: Import the module in an isolated offscreen interpreter and assert no Qt module is loaded (or assert the source imports no PyQt6/pyqtgraph/Qt).
tests.expected_result: Import succeeds without QApplication and without importing PyQt6, pyqtgraph or any Qt module.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given ui/dock_layout.py, When its constants are read, Then CHART_MIN_WIDTH == 400, WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH == 150, DEFAULT_WATCHLIST_WIDTH == 220, RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH == 200, the watchlist cap fraction is 0.50 and the right-dock cap fraction is 0.40, and CHART_MIN_WIDTH is in agreement with ui/watchlist_panel.CHART_MIN_WIDTH.
tests.description: Assert each constant value and cross-check CHART_MIN_WIDTH against the watchlist_panel constant.
tests.expected_result: All constants match their specified values and the two CHART_MIN_WIDTH constants agree.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a chart_area_w, When watchlist_max_width(chart_area_w) is called, Then it returns max(WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH, min(floor(0.50 * chart_area_w), chart_area_w - CHART_MIN_WIDTH)).
tests.description: Parameterized chart_area_w values (e.g. 1400, 900, 800, 600, 100) asserting the exact formula result, including the narrow case where the chart-minimum term binds.
tests.expected_result: Every value equals max(150, min(int(chart_area_w*0.50), chart_area_w-400)); never below 150.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a chart_area_w, When right_dock_max_width(chart_area_w) is called, Then it returns max(RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH, min(floor(0.40 * chart_area_w), chart_area_w - CHART_MIN_WIDTH)).
tests.description: Parameterized chart_area_w values (e.g. 1400, 900, 800, 600, 100) asserting the exact formula result, including the narrow case where the chart-minimum term binds.
tests.expected_result: Every value equals max(200, min(int(chart_area_w*0.40), chart_area_w-400)); never below 200.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a chart_area_w and requested left/right widths, When plan_dock_widths(chart_area_w, requested_left, requested_right) is called, Then each returned width is within its own [min, max] cap, and where feasible chart_area_w - left - right >= CHART_MIN_WIDTH; enlarging one requested width forces the other to shrink when the flat caps would starve the chart.
tests.description: Normal case: chart_area_w=1400 with both docks near their maxima; assert caps hold, chart remainder >=400, and increasing requested_left decreases the returned right (and vice-versa).
tests.expected_result: left <= watchlist_max_width(chart_area_w), right <= right_dock_max_width(chart_area_w), chart_area_w-left-right >= 400, and the non-resized dock shrinks when cross-clamping binds.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given the edge cases (a tiny window where the flat cap is below the dock minimum, both docks requested near their individual maxima, and one side requested over budget), When plan_dock_widths is called, Then it never returns a width below the dock minimum, never raises, and returns stable integer widths even when chart_area_w - left - right cannot reach CHART_MIN_WIDTH (the chart minimum yields on an infeasible window; dock minimums win).
tests.description: Call plan_dock_widths on a tiny chart_area_w, with both requests at max, and with one request over budget; assert min bounds, no exception, integer outputs, and the documented precedence when infeasible.
tests.expected_result: No returned width is below its dock minimum; no exception; the infeasible tiny-window case returns the dock minimums without raising.

tasks.title: Re-parameterise the D13 watchlist width helpers to the chart-area denominator (D17 Phase 1)
tasks.description: Re-parameterise ui/watchlist_panel.py so watchlist_max_width / clamp_watchlist_width / load_watchlist_width / save_watchlist_width are measured against the chart area (not the whole window) and delegate to ui/dock_layout as the single source of the cap, preserving the existing one-argument signature shape. Update tests/test_watchlist.py clamp-math assertions to the chart-area cap in lockstep (R28/B1) without changing the D14 double-click semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Given ui/watchlist_panel.py, When watchlist_max_width(chart_area_w) is called, Then it returns the chart-area cap produced by ui.dock_layout.watchlist_max_width (the formula is not duplicated) while keeping a one-argument signature shape.

Given clamp_watchlist_width(width, chart_area_w), load_watchlist_width(settings, chart_area_w) and save_watchlist_width(settings, width, chart_area_w), When called, Then each clamps into [WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH, ui.dock_layout.watchlist_max_width(chart_area_w)] using dock_layout as the cap source.

Given tests/test_watchlist.py, When the clamp-math assertions run, Then watchlist_max_width/clamp_watchlist_width/load_/save_ are asserted against the chart-area denominator (e.g. watchlist_max_width(1400) == 700, narrow-area behaviour, never below 150) and the D14 should_load_on_double_click and panel-emits-symbol tests still pass.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given ui/watchlist_panel.py, When watchlist_max_width(chart_area_w) is called, Then it returns the chart-area cap produced by ui.dock_layout.watchlist_max_width (the formula is not duplicated) while keeping a one-argument signature shape.
tests.description: For several chart_area_w values assert ui.watchlist_panel.watchlist_max_width == ui.dock_layout.watchlist_max_width, and inspect the source to confirm delegation rather than a duplicated formula.
tests.expected_result: The two functions agree for every sampled input; the panel helper delegates to dock_layout.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given clamp_watchlist_width(width, chart_area_w), load_watchlist_width(settings, chart_area_w) and save_watchlist_width(settings, width, chart_area_w), When called, Then each clamps into [WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH, ui.dock_layout.watchlist_max_width(chart_area_w)] using dock_layout as the cap source.
tests.description: Exercise clamp/load/save round-trips over a QSettings INI file with the chart-area denominator; assert clamping at the chart-area cap and the 150px floor, and default ~220px with no saved value.
tests.expected_result: clamp(1e6, area) == dock_layout.watchlist_max_width(area); clamp(0, area) == 150; no saved value loads 220; a saved value is restored clamped to the current cap.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given tests/test_watchlist.py, When the clamp-math assertions run, Then watchlist_max_width/clamp_watchlist_width/load_/save_ are asserted against the chart-area denominator (e.g. watchlist_max_width(1400) == 700, narrow-area behaviour, never below 150) and the D14 should_load_on_double_click and panel-emits-symbol tests still pass.
tests.description: Run the updated tests/test_watchlist.py, confirming the clamp-math assertions now use the chart-area denominator and the D14 tests are unchanged and green.
tests.expected_result: tests/test_watchlist.py passes entirely; no assertion still encodes the old window-width denominator.

tasks.title: Enforce the watchlist cap live during the drag and on resize/full-screen (D17 Phase 2)
tasks.description: In ui/main_window.py add the shared _apply_dock_widths() that reads centralWidget().width() as chart_area and issues resizeDocks for the watchlist, wire it to the dock-area internal QSplitter.splitterMoved hook and a two-directional resizeEvent, re-clamp the persisted width on restore and in closeEvent, guard against recursion/jitter, and keep the deferred splitter acquisition + event-filter fallback per the architecture risk. No right-region changes yet. Update tests/test_d10_d13_integration.py to the chart-area denominator and ship focused offscreen tests.
acceptance_criteria: AC-D17.1: Given a docked Watchlist and a loaded chart, When the user drags the splitter handle to the right, Then the watchlist width grows continuously up to floor(0.50 * chart_area) and the chart area narrows correspondingly; the watchlist width is <= floor(0.50 * chart_area) at all times during and after the drag.

AC-D17.2: Given the watchlist is wider than its minimum, When the user drags the handle to the left, Then the watchlist width reduces continuously down to WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH (150px) and stops there, with the chart area growing correspondingly and the width never going below 150px.

AC-D17.3: Given the app is shown full screen (no window resizeEvent fires during the drag), When the user drags past the cap, Then the width stops at the cap during the drag itself (the splitterMoved hook enforces it) with no overshoot into the chart and no later resizeEvent required.

AC-D17.4: Given a Watchlist width persisted by a previous session, When the app restarts, Then the width is restored as the persisted integer pixel value clamped to the current floor(0.50 * chart_area) and the chart minimum (default ~220px if none saved, never <150px).

AC-D17.5: Given the watchlist is at/near its cap, When the available chart-area width shrinks (main window narrowed), Then the watchlist is re-clamped to the new cap without error and remains resizable; the same re-clamp is invoked from the shared _apply_dock_widths so the right region can drive it later.

Given _apply_dock_widths, When it issues resizeDocks, Then it is re-entrancy-guarded (a guard flag / blockSignals) and only calls resizeDocks when the computed size differs from the current size by more than 1px, so an applied resize does not recurse and produces no jitter.

Given the updated tests/test_d10_d13_integration.py, When it runs, Then its clamp assertions use the chart-area denominator (never the old window-width formula) and the D10 volume-toggle behaviour assertions remain green.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D17.1: Given a docked Watchlist and a loaded chart, When the user drags the splitter handle to the right, Then the watchlist width grows continuously up to floor(0.50 * chart_area) and the chart area narrows correspondingly; the watchlist width is <= floor(0.50 * chart_area) at all times during and after the drag.
tests.description: Offscreen MainWindow with IBApiClient.connect monkeypatched; drive the splitterMoved/_apply_dock_widths path to a large requested watchlist width and assert the effective dock width == floor(0.50 * chart_area) and the central chart area narrowed.
tests.expected_result: Watchlist width equals the chart-area cap (<= floor(0.50*chart_area)) and centralWidget().width() decreased versus the pre-drag value.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D17.2: Given the watchlist is wider than its minimum, When the user drags the handle to the left, Then the watchlist width reduces continuously down to WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH (150px) and stops there, with the chart area growing correspondingly and the width never going below 150px.
tests.description: Drive the width request down through intermediate values and a below-minimum request; assert monotone decrease and a floor at 150px.
tests.expected_result: Watchlist width decreases with each leftward step and never falls below WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D17.3: Given the app is shown full screen (no window resizeEvent fires during the drag), When the user drags past the cap, Then the width stops at the cap during the drag itself (the splitterMoved hook enforces it) with no overshoot into the chart and no later resizeEvent required.
tests.description: Show the window, simulate a drag past the cap by invoking the splitterMoved handler directly without any window resize, and assert the effective width is the cap rather than the pre-clamp request.
tests.expected_result: After the drag hook runs with no resizeEvent, watchlist width == floor(0.50*chart_area), not the oversized request.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D17.4: Given a Watchlist width persisted by a previous session, When the app restarts, Then the width is restored as the persisted integer pixel value clamped to the current floor(0.50 * chart_area) and the chart minimum (default ~220px if none saved, never <150px).
tests.description: Seed QSettings watchlist/width with a large value, construct MainWindow, and assert the applied width is the chart-area cap; separately assert the default (~220) with no saved value and the 150px floor.
tests.expected_result: A persisted large width is restored clamped to the current chart-area cap; no saved value yields ~220px; the result is never below 150px.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D17.5: Given the watchlist is at/near its cap, When the available chart-area width shrinks (main window narrowed), Then the watchlist is re-clamped to the new cap without error and remains resizable; the same re-clamp is invoked from the shared _apply_dock_widths so the right region can drive it later.
tests.description: Set the watchlist to the cap for a wide window, shrink the window, and assert the watchlist is re-clamped to the new (smaller) cap without error and can still be resized.
tests.expected_result: After the shrink the watchlist width <= the new chart-area cap and no exception is raised.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given _apply_dock_widths, When it issues resizeDocks, Then it is re-entrancy-guarded (a guard flag / blockSignals) and only calls resizeDocks when the computed size differs from the current size by more than 1px, so an applied resize does not recurse and produces no jitter.
tests.description: Spy on resizeDocks across repeated _apply_dock_widths invocations at a fixed geometry and assert it is a no-op when unchanged; assert re-entrant calls are suppressed.
tests.expected_result: Repeated applies at the same geometry do not re-issue resizeDocks; no recursion/stack growth or jitter.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given the updated tests/test_d10_d13_integration.py, When it runs, Then its clamp assertions use the chart-area denominator (never the old window-width formula) and the D10 volume-toggle behaviour assertions remain green.
tests.description: Run tests/test_d10_d13_integration.py after updating the denominator assertions and confirm volume hide/show plus the chart-minimum coupling still pass.
tests.expected_result: tests/test_d10_d13_integration.py passes with chart-area-denominator assertions and unchanged D10 assertions.

tasks.title: Reshape Active Trader + Portfolio into one right-dock region (D18 Phase 3)

Keep ladder/portfolio behaviour and signals untouched; add no width cap yet. Update the right-dock lookup tests in lockstep where they seek the now-absent 'Portfolio' dock.
acceptance_criteria: AC-D18.3: Given the single right region is visible, Then the Active Trader ladder section and the Portfolio section render at equal width within a 1px tolerance, each equal to the region's content width, because they are stacked sections of one region.

Given ui/main_window.py after the reshape, When findChild(QDockWidget, 'Active Trader') is called, Then it returns the single right region (stable title and objectName) so _on_dom_toggled still toggles it, and there is exactly one QDockWidget in RightDockWidgetArea on the right side.
Given the reshape, When the ladder/portfolio order-entry, summary and signal wiring are inspected, Then no ladder/portfolio behaviour or signal connection changed (only the container around them).

Given the updated right-dock lookup tests, When they run, Then tests/test_crosshair_axis_lane.py resolves the single right region and asserts the D2 chip does not intersect it, and the tolerant hide-by-title loops in tests/test_d10_d13_integration.py, tests/test_watchlist_d14_midrag.py and tests/test_history_backfill*.py are green (updated to the single-region shape where they referenced the removed 'Portfolio' dock).

tasks.title: Add the right-region 40% cap, cross-clamp, content bound and full-screen normalize (D18 Phase 4)
tasks.description: Wire the single right region into the shared MainWindow._apply_dock_widths so it grows to floor(0.40 * chart_area), shrinks to its minimum, and cross-clamps with the watchlist via plan_dock_widths so chart_area >= 400px; add the changeEvent(WindowStateChange) + resizeEvent full-screen normalize (no showFullScreen), keep the region unpersisted, and bound the minimum/ideal width of ui/active_trader_panel.py and ui/active_portfolio_panel.py so their tables scroll/clip internally and content cannot push the region off-screen. Ship focused offscreen tests.
acceptance_criteria: AC-D18.2: Given the right region is visible, When the user enlarges it, Then its width grows up to floor(0.40 * chart_area) and the chart area narrows correspondingly; the region width is <= floor(0.40 * chart_area) during and after the resize.

AC-D18.4: Given the right region is at/near its cap, When the user drags further to enlarge, Then the width stops at the cap with no overshoot; When the user drags to shrink, Then the region reduces down to RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH and stops, never below the minimum.

AC-D18.5: Given both the watchlist and the right region are enlarged, When their combined width would push the chart area below its ~400px minimum, Then both docks are clamped so chart_area stays >= 400px and enlarging one forces the other to shrink rather than letting the chart collapse.

AC-D18.1: Given the app is shown full screen, When the chart and the right region render, Then the right region is fully within the visible window area (its geometry lies within the window rect and its width is > 0) without manual repositioning, via the changeEvent(WindowStateChange)/resizeEvent normalize step.

AC-D18.6: Given the ladder/portfolio content is wider than the region, When the region renders, Then the region's geometry still satisfies the visibility and cap assertions (content minimums do not force it past the window edge or past the cap) because each panel's width is bounded and its tables scroll/clip internally.
AC-D18.7: Given the app restarts, Then the right region's width/visibility is not persisted (no new QSettings key is added; the default applies), matching D10's volume-toggle precedent.

Given the right region is wired into _apply_dock_widths alongside the watchlist, When the widths are applied, Then there is no recursion/jitter between the two regions' rescale (re-entrancy guard and only-resize-when-changed both hold).

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D18.2: Given the right region is visible, When the user enlarges it, Then its width grows up to floor(0.40 * chart_area) and the chart area narrows correspondingly; the region width is <= floor(0.40 * chart_area) during and after the resize.
tests.description: Offscreen MainWindow; enlarge the right region via the resize/apply path and assert the effective region width == floor(0.40 * chart_area) and centralWidget().width() decreased.
tests.expected_result: Right-region width equals the 40% chart-area cap and the chart area narrowed.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D18.4: Given the right region is at/near its cap, When the user drags further to enlarge, Then the width stops at the cap with no overshoot; When the user drags to shrink, Then the region reduces down to RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH and stops, never below the minimum.
tests.description: Drive the right region over-cap and below-min requests and assert clamping at floor(0.40*chart_area) and RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH respectively.
tests.expected_result: No applied width exceeds the cap or falls below the region minimum.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D18.5: Given both the watchlist and the right region are enlarged, When their combined width would push the chart area below its ~400px minimum, Then both docks are clamped so chart_area stays >= 400px and enlarging one forces the other to shrink rather than letting the chart collapse.
tests.description: Set both docks near their individual maxima, then enlarge one via the shared apply path; assert centralWidget().width() >= 400 and the other dock's width decreased.
tests.expected_result: chart_area >= 400px after the enlargement and the non-resized dock shrank.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D18.1: Given the app is shown full screen, When the chart and the right region render, Then the right region is fully within the visible window area (its geometry lies within the window rect and its width is > 0) without manual repositioning, via the changeEvent(WindowStateChange)/resizeEvent normalize step.
tests.description: Show a full-screen-sized offscreen window, deliver a WindowStateChange/changeEvent and resize, process the deferred singleShot normalize, and assert the right region geometry is inside the window rect with width > 0.
tests.expected_result: The right region's geometry is contained by the window rect and its width is positive.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: AC-D18.6: Given the ladder/portfolio content is wider than the region, When the region renders, Then the region's geometry still satisfies the visibility and cap assertions (content minimums do not force it past the window edge or past the cap) because each panel's width is bounded and its tables scroll/clip internally.
tests.description: Populate the ladder/portfolio tables with wide content, render, and assert the region width/right edge still satisfy the cap and visibility assertions.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given the right region is wired into _apply_dock_widths alongside the watchlist, When the widths are applied, Then there is no recursion/jitter between the two regions' rescale (re-entrancy guard and only-resize-when-changed both hold).

tasks.title: Fix plan_dock_widths to never return below a dock minimum, add the one-sided-over-budget regression test, and remove the T49 MainWindow workaround (ESC-026)
tasks.description: Correct ui/dock_layout.py::plan_dock_widths so its shrink loop re-floors left/right at WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH/RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH (its docstring guarantee and AC-D18.4) instead of decrementing below a dock minimum on a one-sided over-budget request; add the missing regression test for the reproduced cases plan_dock_widths(750, 100000, 200) and (750, 200, 0); then remove the now-redundant T49 in-place repair in MainWindow._plan_dock_widths so ui/dock_layout.py is again the single source of truth. No acceptance criterion or architecture change — the AC and architecture are correct; only the pure helper's shrink loop and the workaround are wrong.
acceptance_criteria: Given plan_dock_widths is called with any integer chart_area_w and requested left/right widths, When either returned width is compared to its dock minimum, Then left >= WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH (150) and right >= RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH (200) in every case, including the one-sided over-budget and both-requested-over-budget cases.

Given the reproduced one-sided over-budget inputs plan_dock_widths(750, 100000, 200) and plan_dock_widths(750, 200, 0), When the function is called, Then (left, right) >= (150, 200) componentwise and neither width drops below its dock minimum (returning e.g. (350, 0) or (175, 175) is a failure).

Given an infeasible window where the two dock minimums alone exceed chart_area_w - CHART_MIN_WIDTH, When plan_dock_widths is called, Then the chart minimum yields and the function returns exactly (WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH, RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH); where the window is feasible but the combined request exceeds budget, the chart minimum is preserved (chart_area_w - left - right >= CHART_MIN_WIDTH) and the reserved chart minimum yields before any dock minimum is crossed.

Given MainWindow._plan_dock_widths after the T49 in-place repair is removed, When the shared dock-width apply path runs (including cross-clamp and over-cap/under-min drags), Then plan_dock_widths is the single source of truth and the resulting widths still satisfy the D18 cap (right <= floor(0.40 * chart_area)) and cross-clamp (chart area >= CHART_MIN_WIDTH) guarantees, so the earlier T49/T50 acceptance tests still pass.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given plan_dock_widths is called with any integer chart_area_w and requested left/right widths, When either returned width is compared to its dock minimum, Then left >= WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH (150) and right >= RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH (200) in every case, including the one-sided over-budget and both-requested-over-budget cases.
tests.description: Property/enumeration test over a grid of chart_area_w values and requested left/right extremes (including 0 and huge values) asserting every returned left >= WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH and right >= RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH.
tests.expected_result: No grid combination yields a left below 150 or a right below 200; the pre-fix coarse grid's 108/1475 violations are all gone.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given the reproduced one-sided over-budget inputs plan_dock_widths(750, 100000, 200) and plan_dock_widths(750, 200, 0), When the function is called, Then (left, right) >= (150, 200) componentwise and neither width drops below its dock minimum (returning e.g. (350, 0) or (175, 175) is a failure).
tests.description: Regression test for the exact reproduced cases: plan_dock_widths(750, 100000, 200) and plan_dock_widths(750, 200, 0); assert each returned width >= its dock minimum.
tests.expected_result: plan_dock_widths(750, 100000, 200) returns left >= 150 and right >= 200; plan_dock_widths(750, 200, 0) returns left >= 150 and right >= 200 (not (350, 0) / (175, 175)).

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given an infeasible window where the two dock minimums alone exceed chart_area_w - CHART_MIN_WIDTH, When plan_dock_widths is called, Then the chart minimum yields and the function returns exactly (WATCHLIST_MIN_WIDTH, RIGHT_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH); where the window is feasible but the combined request exceeds budget, the chart minimum is preserved (chart_area_w - left - right >= CHART_MIN_WIDTH) and the reserved chart minimum yields before any dock minimum is crossed.
tests.description: Assert documented precedence: an infeasible chart_area_w (e.g. 400 with both requests high) returns exactly the dock minimums; a feasible over-budget case (e.g. chart_area_w=1000, requests at their flat caps) preserves chart_area_w - left - right >= CHART_MIN_WIDTH while both widths stay >= their minimums.
tests.expected_result: Infeasible window returns (150, 200); feasible over-budget case keeps chart remainder >= 400 with both widths at/above their minimums, matching the unchanged docstring guarantee.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given MainWindow._plan_dock_widths after the T49 in-place repair is removed, When the shared dock-width apply path runs (including cross-clamp and over-cap/under-min drags), Then plan_dock_widths is the single source of truth and the resulting widths still satisfy the D18 cap (right <= floor(0.40 * chart_area)) and cross-clamp (chart area >= CHART_MIN_WIDTH) guarantees, so the earlier T49/T50 acceptance tests still pass.
tests.description: Offscreen MainWindow test (no live TWS) driving the shared apply path after the T49 repair is removed: grow the right dock to its cap and shrink below its minimum, and cross-clamp both docks; assert right <= floor(0.40*chart_area), each dock >= its minimum, and chart area >= CHART_MIN_WIDTH, i.e. the D18 guarantees now rest solely on plan_dock_widths.
tests.expected_result: The MainWindow path (with the repair removed) still enforces the 40% cap, the dock minimums and the chart-area cross-clamp; the retained T49/T50 tests remain green.
